question: Do streams written with matrices, noise channels, bypassed bits, output shifts and channel assignments decode to the samples they were written from, in this decoder and in decoders that share nothing with it; and where the decoders part, what does each of them do?
method: crates/oadec-synth now writes what lies over the channels of a 0x31EA substream and undoes it: from the samples of a recipe it takes off the output shift and inverts each matrix, the last first, with the noise the decoder will draw. tools/synth_accept.py runs FFmpeg, `truehdd` and Dolby's decoder (the `dlbtruehddec` element of the Dolby Reference Player, on the stream wrapped in MP4, TrueHD syntax only) on every recipe as in evidence 10, and compares what each writes with the samples of the recipe byte for byte. Where a decoder gave other samples, streams of one matrix each were written to find the rule: every arrangement of a quantiser step, a matrix and a bypassed bit, and of the two noise channels, their shift and their register. For the step with a bypassed bit, three readings of the decoding were computed from the samples of the stream and counted against what Dolby's decoder wrote. The matrices in force in the blocks of real streams were counted with the segment parser of the decoder, a callback seeing every block with the state in force after its header, over the 41 TrueHD streams and five clips of the work directory and the nine committed fixtures. Ten mutations of what the decoder does over the channels (tools/mutants.py) were run against the suite of the commit this branch starts from, which has the 26 recipes of evidence 10, against the suite of this branch, and against the tests over the recipes alone, every test run to its end.

reading: The writer can now be told what lies over the channels, and the 12 recipes that say so come back from this decoder and from the outside ones: 10 of them from every decoder asked. The noise channels are the part of this syntax no real stream uses, and the three outside decoders draw the same noise from the same register at a shift of 0, FFmpeg and Dolby's decoder at any shift; truehdd parts from them when the noise is shifted, on the evidence of its own lossless check. The other exception is of another weight. A matrix that has both a quantiser step to cut to and a bypassed bit to add is read one way by FFmpeg, truehdd and this decoder and another way by Dolby's: on four streams written to separate the readings, `sum + bit` gives every sample Dolby's decoder wrote and the cut sum gives 33 to 39 of 640. No real stream can be heard on it: none of 242,812,003 matrices in force in the blocks of 55 streams has both. So the three decoders that agree here agree on something only one more decoder has ever been asked, and that one, the format owner's, says otherwise. This decoder is left where it was: the change would move no sample of any stream that exists, and the recipe records the reading it has with Dolby's decoder named as the one that gave other samples. What the measurement settles is narrower than which reading is right: it is what each decoder does, and that a test on real material could never have shown the difference. The mutations say the same of the suite. Of 10, 2 passed the suite before these recipes, the 26 of evidence 10 in it, and 3 more were caught by one hand-built unit test alone; with the recipes all are caught, every one of them by the decode of a written stream alone.
